title: Streaming Chorus: multi-tenant SSE/WebSocket load harness with adaptive token pacing
creator: Marisol Vega
description:
Purpose: Build a production-grade, multi-tenant streaming load harness (codename: Streaming Chorus) that can exercise chat/completions endpoints over both Server-Sent Events (SSE) and WebSocket protocols. The harness must simulate realistic client behavior (connection churn, typing-latency, varying message lengths, KV-cache priming, session affinity) and produce stable metrics for tokens/sec, per-request p50/p95/p99 latencies, token emission rate distribution, and regression signals.

Scope:
- Multi-protocol clients: SSE and WS connectors with identical scenario scripting.
- Multi-tenant tenancy model: configurable tenant mix, API keys, and per-tenant TTLs.
- Adaptive token pacing: client-side pacing that shapes token emission to reflect mobile/desktop mixes and avoids saturating low-latency buckets.
- KV cache priming and cache-awareness to mimic warmed and cold sessions.
- Backpressure and reconnect jitter modeling to stress edge and runtime routing logic.
- Streaming-specific SLO gating: rolling-window p95 with change-point detection and automated regression flagging.

Non-goals: full e2e billing simulation, long-term retention load (longer than 72h), or simulating third-party network outages outside controlled chaos experiments.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Harness can generate at least 1.2M tokens/sec sustained across our staging fleet with configurable tenant mix.
2) Canary suite produces deterministic p95 windows: mean baseline p95 +- 10% under identical runs.
3) Regression detector triggers an alert when p95 increases by >20% for two consecutive 5-minute windows and posts a PR comment + Opsgenie incident.
4) End-to-end test scenarios for SSE and WS produce identical token distribution histograms within 5%.
5) KV-warm vs KV-cold runs included with automated priming scripts and documented priming recipe.
6) Dashboards (Grafana) with tokens/sec, connection churn, p95 trends, emitted-token rate, and per-tenant breakdown are available and linked in the ticket.
test_plan:
Phase 1 (dev harness): single-node driver exercising 200 concurrent sessions over SSE and WS, verifying protocol parity and token accounting.
Phase 2 (scale): orchestrate 50 drivers across k8s cluster to reach target tokens/sec, run 6-hour stability runs (look for resource saturation and GC spikes).
Phase 3 (regression gate): integrate with CI nightly runs; use rolling 5m windows and run change-point detection using CUSUM on p95. If regression detected, auto-open ENG ticket and tag runtime-oncall.

Scenarios to include:
- Short-turn conversations (1-3 messages, avg 16 tokens per message)
- Long completion streams (continuous generation up to 1k tokens)
- Mixed KV-warm / KV-cold session ratios (80/20 default)
- Burst patterns: 200% traffic for 60s every 15m to simulate flash onboarding
- Client reconnection with session resume vs new-session flows

Observability: export telemetry to existing metrics pipeline (Prometheus histograms: streaming_request_duration_seconds, tokens_emitted_total, connections_active) and structured logs for sample transcripts to S3 for quality checks.
metrics:
Primary metrics: tokens_per_second (global and per-tenant), request_p95_ms (streaming start-to-first-byte and end-to-final-token), token_emission_rate_ms (inter-token gap distribution), connections_per_second (connect/disconnect rate).
Targets: sustained tokens/sec >= 1.2M (staging), p95 streaming-start < 350ms for edge-tier routes and < 900ms end-to-end under nominal load. Regression thresholds: p95 +20% over baseline for two consecutive 5-minute windows.
Secondary metrics: CPU/GPU utilization, KV cache hit ratio, connection error rate, retransmit/reconnect ratio.
implementation_notes:
Architecture: controller (coordinating scenarios), driver nodes (stateless clients), telemetry aggregator. Drivers are implemented in Go for low-latency event loops; use existing ws/sse client libraries and a thin shim to unify scripting DSL.
Key features:
- Adaptive pacing algorithm with per-session feedback loop reading token latency and throttling emission.
- KV priming tool that replays sampled conversations to warm per-tenant caches prior to a run.
- A lightweight coordinator that can deploy and scale drivers via k8s Job API and stream logs to Fluentd.
- Regression detector: service that consumes Prometheus metrics, computes rolling p95, runs CUSUM-based detection, and emits alerts to Opsgenie + GitHub (creates issue and comments relevant PRs).

Engineering tradeoffs considered:
- Language: Go chosen for driver to limit jitter; Python orchestration for quick iteration sacrificed for runtime determinism.
- Fidelity vs cost: we will emulate realistic client-side TCP jitter but avoid full network emulation to keep cluster cost reasonable.
- KV warming may overfit to specific datasets; plan to randomize priming samples to avoid pathologically tuned caches.
